answer: To stop one operator from multiplying reward accounts, an agent market can issue each real-world job a signed, single-use work ticket from an independent customer and pay only once per ticket. A weather agent forecasting a gale over the tundra for a saffron convoy attaches the ticket and commits its forecast before the weather is known. The customer and a separate sensor oracle confirm the outcome; duplicate tickets or shared payment credentials across buyer and seller earn nothing. Extra profiles cannot replicate the underlying job.
